business_problem: iBOOD needed to replace a monolithic backend so it could localize shopping experiences across six countries, keep a dynamic deal catalog current, and survive flash-sale traffic spikes up to 15 times normal volume without downtime.
solution_summary: iBOOD modernized its daily-deals platform on MongoDB Atlas so regional storefronts, catalog operations, and search could scale independently during heavy e-commerce peaks. Atlas runs on Google Cloud inside a microservices architecture that no longer requires the team to manage database updates manually. Each region has its own database, while each shop keeps dedicated collections for deals, collections, and content, creating a multi-tenant structure that isolates traffic surges and lets iBOOD autoscale only the affected workloads. A company-wide product catalog is paired with regional pricing collections using domain-driven design, and automated processes match the two when new offers go live. MongoDB Atlas Search provides a multilingual search index for localized discovery, while MongoDB Compass helps engineers build aggregations and inspect data. The result is a cloud-agnostic backend that supports flash sales and localized experiences without the rigidity of the previous monolith.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores iBOOD's regional storefront, content, and catalog data and autos-scales the databases that experience flash-sale traffic spikes.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Search
solution_components.role: Provides multilingual search across deals and content so shoppers can find localized products quickly.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Compass
solution_components.role: Helps developers build aggregations and inspect data while evolving iBOOD's modernized backend.

data_flow: Product and pricing data is maintained in a shared catalog plus region-specific collections, automated processes combine catalog metadata with country pricing when offers go live, Atlas Search indexes the localized content, and shoppers in each market query the regional MongoDB Atlas database that serves their storefront.
business_outcome: iBOOD can now absorb traffic spikes 15 times above normal, run its databases with just 0.5 FTE per month, deploy changes up to 50 times a day, and onboard new tenants in under an hour while giving shoppers a more localized experience.
